title: [RFC] Define the AL2023 runtime contract and redistribution policy
scope: Settle the initial static/base contract before rootfs implementation. Start with official AL2023 packages and a BuildKit multi-stage builder, with scratch final images. Decide file boundaries, glibc/NSS behavior, CA paths, UTC/locale policy, non-root identity, supported workloads, and package-license/source handling.
acceptance: Record accepted static/base contents and exclusions, including whether base contains OpenSSL libraries
Specify UID/GID 65532, working directory, /tmp permissions, read-only-rootfs behavior, CA bundle paths, NSS configuration, UTC, and locale behavior
Document compatible AL2023-linked workloads and limitations for arbitrary glibc or musl binaries
Choose verified RPM extraction or installroot assembly and document scriptlet/configuration handling
Define project licensing versus redistributed RPM licenses, notices, and source-availability obligations
Review the proposed architecture and record unresolved risks as follow-up issues
validation: Design review against official AL2023 package metadata and at least one static Go and one dynamic C workload. Record a decision, rationale, and evidence in docs/.

title: [Task] Lock AL2023 builder and RPM inputs with provenance
scope: Create a versioned input lock and resolver for official AL2023 packages. Pin a builder index digest separately from the DNF releasever. Capture architecture-specific package versions, checksums, signatures, repository metadata, and license/source references.
acceptance: Pin an official builder digest and an explicit AL2023 releasever; release mode rejects floating latest inputs
Record per-architecture package NEVRAs, checksums, dependency closure, signature verification, and repository references
Disable weak dependencies deliberately and document necessary exceptions
Produce a package-to-file/provenance inventory suitable for final-image SBOM generation
Document a repeatable lock update command and reviewable package diff
validation: Resolve twice only as the reproducibility experiment, compare the locked package set, and prove that a modified checksum or invalid/untrusted signature fails closed.

title: [Task] Assemble amd64 static and base rootfs from verified AL2023 packages
scope: Implement allowlist-driven rootfs assembly and scratch Dockerfile targets for static and base on amd64. Avoid copying the complete builder filesystem. Preserve required licenses, runtime configuration, ownership, and symlinks.
acceptance: Build static and base targets from locked inputs with a documented single entry command
Give every copied file a reviewed source/provenance entry and reject unexpected or missing files
Resolve ELF interpreter and transitive shared-library dependencies, including architecture-specific symlinks
Include the accepted CA/NSS/user/temporary-directory contract and default to numeric non-root UID/GID
Exclude shells, package managers, RPM databases, compilers, and build caches from production outputs
Emit a final file inventory with checksums, modes, ownership, and symlink targets
validation: Inspect an exported final rootfs; compare it with the allowlist and run minimal static and dynamic binaries. Do not use an untrusted binary's ldd execution as the audit mechanism.

title: [Task] Prove the final-image runtime and absent-tool contract
scope: Add meaningful black-box probes against final static/base images: pure static Go and AL2023-linked C, with a local controlled service for DNS/TLS behavior. Keep fixtures separate from production images.
acceptance: Static Go and dynamically linked C probes run in their intended variants with the expected non-root identity
Validate DNS/NSS resolution, CA trust with a controlled TLS endpoint, UTC/time behavior, and passwd/group lookup
Run supported workloads with read-only rootfs, an explicit temporary mount, all capabilities dropped, and no-new-privileges
Assert that shell and package-manager execution is unavailable and inspect the complete rootfs for forbidden tools
Verify exec-form startup, signal handling, and exit-code behavior without assuming a shell or an init binary
Document supported and deliberately unsupported workloads
validation: Run the contract suite on linux/amd64 with a fresh final-image build. Capture exact build inputs and test logs. Use deterministic local test infrastructure rather than public endpoint availability.

title: [Task] Add arm64 builds and architecture-specific runtime validation
scope: Extend the prototype to linux/arm64, with explicit mapping to AL2023 aarch64 packages and loader paths. Support local emulation for convenience and documented native execution for release qualification.
acceptance: Build both static/base variants for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 from locked architecture-correct RPMs
Reject mixed-architecture packages and validate each ELF interpreter and library closure
Pass the same runtime contract on both architectures
Document emulation limitations and obtain native arm64 runtime evidence before stable release
Assemble and inspect an OCI index without publishing production tags
validation: Run per-architecture final-container probes and inspect index platform descriptors. Record whether each execution was native or emulated.

title: [Task] Add unprivileged PR image builds and runtime CI
scope: Build/test changed image definitions on pull requests and main without registry publishing credentials. Keep privileged release work in a separate future workflow.
acceptance: CI covers both variants and supported architectures and uploads useful inventories and test logs
Pull-request jobs use read-only permissions and do not expose release credentials to fork code
Pin action dependencies and document cache keys that include lock inputs and architecture
Add path-aware execution without leaving required checks permanently pending when paths are skipped
Make the implemented build/runtime checks required for main after their first successful runs
Document local commands that reproduce the CI checks
validation: Exercise one passing workload and one intentionally failing fixture in a temporary branch/PR, confirm check behavior, then remove the intentional failure before merge.

title: [Task] Measure reproducibility and establish image-size budgets
scope: Measure normalized rootfs reproducibility separately from image/index digest reproducibility. Establish evidence-based size budgets per variant/architecture against official AL2023 base and minimal baselines.
acceptance: Compare clean builds from identical locked inputs and explain any rootfs differences
Normalize ordering, modes, ownership, timestamps, and archive metadata where supported
Report OCI digest differences caused by provenance or build metadata separately from runtime-file differences
Record compressed transfer size, unpacked size, file count, and package count with measurement definitions
Set reviewed size-regression budgets from measured results rather than guessed size claims
Publish a baseline report and make material regressions visible in CI
validation: Run the documented paired clean-build experiment once for each supported variant/architecture and store the manifest comparison and size report.

title: [Task] Produce SBOM, provenance, and complete redistribution evidence
scope: Generate per-architecture component evidence from the actual included files, preserving AL2023 identity even though the runtime has no RPM database. Cover project and component license obligations.
acceptance: Generate machine-readable SBOMs with exact included package versions, file ownership, checksums, and source references
Distinguish complete installed RPM contents from the subset actually shipped in the runtime
Attach verifiable build provenance covering source commit, builder digest, releasever, tool versions, and lock inputs
Include required license texts/notices and fulfill the accepted source-availability approach
Validate SBOM subjects against final image digests and document consumer retrieval
Test at least one partial-package case so inventory does not falsely claim an entire RPM is present
validation: Inspect the SBOM against the rootfs/package-to-file map, verify digest subjects, and review license/source completeness for every redistributed component.

title: [Task] Add AL2023-aware vulnerability scanning and exception policy
scope: Choose and pin a scanner that recognizes AL2023 package identity from the final image/evidence. Define stable-release gates and a reviewable, expiring exception mechanism.
acceptance: Demonstrate correct AL2023 detection and package versions without a runtime RPM database
Compare representative scanner results with ALAS advisories and backported-fix versions
Fail stable releases on applicable critical/high findings unless a reviewed, scoped, owned, expiring exception exists
Fail closed for scanner/database errors and document database age policy
Record scan tool/database versions, results, applicability decisions, and exception expiry checks
Document false-positive handling without claiming zero CVEs from missing metadata
validation: Use known affected and fixed AL2023 package fixtures plus expired/valid exception fixtures to demonstrate gate behavior.

title: [Task] Publish signed immutable multi-architecture GHCR releases
scope: Agree on the image/tag naming scheme and implement trusted release promotion to GHCR for static/base. Proposed paths are ghcr.io/rambow-cloud/amazon-linux-distroless/static and /base; validate package permissions and naming before adopting them.
acceptance: Document image names, versioned tags, optional moving aliases, digest consumption, prereleases, and immutability policy
Publish only after all required per-architecture checks, size gates, evidence generation, and scans pass
Restrict release inputs to reviewed protected-branch commits and validate tag/commit relationships
Sign image/index subjects using a documented identity and publish retrievable SBOM/provenance evidence
Use least-privilege publishing/OIDC permissions and prevent untrusted PR code from obtaining them
Test consumer signature/provenance verification and rejection of an unexpected identity
Document failed-publication recovery and rollback to a previous verified digest
validation: Perform a tagged prerelease/candidate end-to-end before any stable release. Verify both platform pulls, index signatures, evidence subjects, access permissions, and documented rollback.

title: [Task] Automate reviewed AL2023 refreshes and document support policy
scope: Implement a reviewed update-detection process for upstream repository/builder changes, security fixes, and pinned tooling. Define achievable maintenance commitments before stable release.
acceptance: Detect upstream AL2023 release and digest changes and create a scoped update issue or PR without silently publishing
Include package/version/license/size diffs and relevant ALAS security impact in update proposals
Run the full release evidence and runtime gates on refreshes
Document supported tags, maintenance window, update cadence, vulnerability triage expectations, and end-of-life handling
Distinguish upstream AL2023/package support from this project's own support commitments
Document rollback and emergency fix procedures; avoid promising an unstaffed response SLA
validation: Exercise the detector with a controlled old/new lock fixture, confirm duplicate detection, and walk through one candidate refresh and rollback. No schedule is enabled until the implementation is reviewed.

title: [Task] Deliver consumer examples and v1.0 release acceptance evidence
scope: Document how consumers build applications against the runtime contract, pin digests, verify evidence, and operate without a shell. Collect a stable-release acceptance checklist.
acceptance: Provide tested static Go and dynamic C multi-stage examples for both architectures
Show exec-form entrypoints, non-root operation, read-only rootfs, writable mounts, and digest pinning
Document CA/NSS/timezone/locale behavior, compatibility boundaries, debugging approach, and troubleshooting
Provide copyable signature/SBOM/provenance verification instructions tied to the actual release identity
Publish a v1.0 acceptance report with native runtime evidence on both architectures, size baselines, scan results, and support policy
Remove planning-only placeholders and clearly identify any deferred optional functionality
validation: Build and run every published example against candidate release digests and follow the verification instructions from a clean consumer environment.

title: [Feature] Add an explicitly scoped AL2023 C++ runtime variant
scope: Add a separately documented cc variant only after the stable base contract. Include verified libstdc++/libgcc dependencies without introducing compiler toolchains.
acceptance: Accept the cc contract and exact runtime library closure through a linked design decision
Build/test a representative AL2023-linked C++ workload on both architectures
Keep production images shell-free, package-manager-free, and non-root
Extend size, SBOM, licensing, vulnerability, signing, and update gates to cc
Document ABI boundaries and the incremental maintenance/size cost
validation: Run C++ ABI/runtime fixtures and the common final-image contract suite, then inspect the library and license diff from base.

title: [RFC] Define isolated debugging without expanding production images
scope: Compare ephemeral debug containers with an explicitly separate debug image. Do not add a shell to production static/base images.
acceptance: Compare approaches for local Docker and Kubernetes with concrete debugging scenarios
Define access, tool provenance, component licenses, architecture coverage, image size, and update ownership
Document a clear distinction between production images and any separate debug artifacts
Verify troubleshooting steps without requiring production image modification
Record an accepted choice or explicitly defer debug-image publication
validation: Demonstrate a failed-startup or DNS/TLS troubleshooting scenario using the proposed isolated approach.

title: [RFC] Evaluate language runtime demand and maintenance feasibility
scope: Evaluate requests for Java, Python, or Node.js images as separate proposals. Assess official AL2023 package availability, supported versions, ABI behavior, extension modules, and maintenance cost. This issue does not commit to shipping a language image.
acceptance: Collect concrete workloads and select at most one initial runtime proposal, or record a decision to defer
Check per-runtime upstream and AL2023 package support lifecycles against a proposed project support window
Inventory runtime-loaded files/modules and native-extension compatibility requirements
Estimate size, security, licensing, CI, and ongoing update obligations
Create a scoped implementation issue only after an accepted runtime contract and a maintainer commitment
validation: Produce a feasibility report grounded in official package metadata and a minimal workload experiment if a runtime is selected.
